note: Human validation of benchmark ground truth. 3 independent annotators, 30 blind items (12 resolvable, 8 ambiguous, 10 semantic_resolvable), scored against the hidden generator key by scripts/score_human_validation.py. Annotators saw only what a merger sees (ancestor + both branches' value/source/confidence), never the generator's label.
key_findings: On resolvable conflicts the majority human follows the source/confidence signal 12/12 (always picks the high-confidence branch), validating the benchmark's core design assumption.

All 4 resolvable human-vs-generator mismatches are exactly the deliberate 15%-noise items (ground truth set to the low-confidence branch); humans are not wrong, the labels are intentionally noisy -- validating the noise parameter.

The single semantic_resolvable disagreement (gift/no-pet) is a defeasible-constraint family that 2/3 annotators flag, corroborating the constraint-strength construct-validity finding (Appendix on selective resolution).
Ambiguous items: 100% human agreement that no single answer exists.
